Maya (People Ops): Quick thread about Zara. She's transferring H-1B from previous employer and wants to start 2026-06-01. Confirm docs and timing.
Connor (Manager): We're set to onboard her into the infra team. Any blocking visa stuff?
Zara (Candidate): My attorney filed H-1B transfer (no cap). I have an approval notice from prior employer and a valid passport. I can present H-1B approval + I-94; does that let me start immediately?
Priya (Immigration Counsel): For H-1B portability, if the new employer files H-1B petition and it is receipted, the candidate can sometimes start based on receipt if USCIS rules permit; however, presenting a valid H-1B approval from prior employer with a valid I-94 may suffice only if change of employer not required. Best to have current approval (I-797) and I-94 that shows validity. If previous employer's I-94 shows current validity, the worker may need new petition approval for portability rules. I'll review specifics of documents.
Ravi (Payroll): For I-9, H-1B approval notice + unexpired foreign passport + I-94 are acceptable List A documents. We need to retain copies. If new employer files for a petition and we rely on receipt, we need legal sign-off.
Leah (Benefits): H-1B status is fine for benefits eligibility. Enrollment can proceed with hire date 6/1. If there is any gap in authorization, payroll must be notified.
Zara (Candidate): I have my I-797 approval from previous employer and valid passport. My attorney says we should be ok to start while transfer is pending because I'm in H-1B status currently.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Confirming: if Zara's current I-94 shows H-1B status valid through date X and the employer files a new petition, she remains authorized to work for the current employer but switching employers usually requires work to stop until new petition receipt is in hand, unless portability rules apply and the new employer's receipt is available. Many clients choose to have the candidate wait until the new petition is receipted or approved. I recommend we collect the current I-797/I-94 and have the attorney confirm portability eligibility.
Maya (People Ops): Action plan: 1) Zara to upload I-797 and I-94. 2) Priya to confirm portability vs need-for-receipt. 3) Ravi to confirm I-9 docs checklist and payroll start paperwork. 4) Leah to prepare benefits enrollment materials.
Zara (Candidate): Uploaded docs to portal. My attorney also sent notes saying porting should be fine and receipt will be issued within a few days.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Received docs. Zara's I-94 shows end date 2026-09-10 and the I-797 is employer-specific. Given that Zara is in valid H-1B status, she can start with us if the petition we file will be a change of employer; typical safe approach is wait for our petition's receipt notice and then rely on portability rule if attorney confirms. I'll confirm with external counsel.
Ravi (Payroll): Once we have copies of I-797 + I-94, I can process payroll for 6/1. If portability requires a receipt, we need receipt before payroll. Please confirm by Tues.
Connor (Manager): We can be flexible by a week if needed.
Leah (Benefits): I'll set benefits effective 6/1. If we need to shift, we can backdate if necessary.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Quick finalize: external counsel confirms portability allowed on receipt. But because Zara's current I-797/I-94 are valid, and if she prefers to start immediately and sign new offer, we can onboard 6/1 but need our petition receipt within a few days to be safe. I'll mark as "proceed with receipt follow-up".
Maya (People Ops): Great. Zara 1 let's proceed 6/1. Please keep your attorney looped and email receipt when available. Ravi I'll assign payroll ticket to check retention docs.
security-bot: Reminder: do not post scanned copies in slack. Use secure portal.
Zara (Candidate): Thanks everyone! Looking forward to starting 6/1.
Maya (People Ops): Closing 1 saved checklist to onboarding drive.
